conceptual assets.information: The words stored in the processor-internal memory, initialized from the application image in ROM mode or written through the bus in RAM mode, are the values returned for addressed reads. Memory operation and the consuming processor depend on these stored words.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality: application code or data in the memory can be secret and is exposed through bus_rsp_o.data via rdata at lines 81, 95, 128-131, 159-162, and 185. Integrity: the stored words are sensitive memory state and the RAM branches accept bus_req_i.data into the byte memories at lines 116-125 and 145-154. Availability: the memory is required to service reads, while rden gates bus_rsp_o.data at line 185 and the acknowledge is generated at lines 178-180, allowing the transfer to be withheld.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue reads to observe memory contents, issue writes in RAM mode to replace words, or suppress the read response so required words are not transferred.

conceptual assets.information: The address selecting which internal memory word is read or written determines the target of each memory access.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: the access address is sensitive control information because changing it can redirect a read or write to the wrong memory word, as it is copied at line 101 and used to index memory at lines 116-131 and 145-162.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter bus_req_i.addr so that an access fetches or overwrites a different memory word than intended.

conceptual assets.information: The registered rden decision determines whether the internally produced read word is released on the response data port. It has no entry or exit port because it is generated from request fields and only gates the read response.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Availability: rden is assigned from the request at line 176 and gates bus_rsp_o.data at line 185, so the IP can withhold a required memory-read transfer.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the request qualification to produce an inactive rden and thereby block the memory data response.

considered, not kept.reason: Clock and reset inputs and their reset actions are excluded conceptual assets under the explicit clock/reset rule (lines 28-29 and 170-175).
IMEM_SIZE, IMEM_INIT, alt_style_c, and derived implementation constants only select or size the build and cannot be changed or withheld at runtime (lines 24-25, 38, and 41).

The strobe, read/write direction, and byte enables only describe the access and are not pieces of information of their own under the access-command rule, apart from the separately kept read-data release decision (lines 114-125, 143-154, and 176-180).
The acknowledge repeats the request handshake and the error flag is tied to a constant, so neither is information of its own (lines 174-186).
